summary: Describes the AM domain as the official Internet top-level domain of Armenia. It is an informational note about that country-code domain.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC describes Armenia's .AM domain and how names could be registered. It explains the flat naming structure and two registration methods.

questions: what is the am top level domain
how does am domain registration work
subtitle: Registration and naming rules for Armenia's .AM top-level domain.

tldr.problem: The memo describes the structure and registration process for Armenia's official Internet top-level domain.
tldr.mechanism: It allows direct registration under .AM, permits subdomains, reserves MIL.AM and GOV.AM, and describes delegation and direct registration.
tldr.outcome: The memo identifies the AM Network Information Center as the registry handling registrations.

today: RFC 2053 is Informational and describes the .AM domain and its registration process as recorded in the memo.

sections.title: The .AM Top-Level Domain
sections.content:
The RFC identifies .AM as the official Internet top-level domain of Armenia. It says AM is the ISO 3166 two-letter country code for the Republic of Armenia and that the domain is registered like other country domains.

The memo names the AM Network Information Center as Armenia's national Internet registry and registration administrator.
sections.plainLanguage: .AM is the top-level Internet domain for Armenia. The AM Network Information Center handles registrations.

sections.title: Naming Structure and Reserved Domains
sections.content:
The .AM hierarchy is flat: an organization may register directly under the top-level domain, as in the example arminco.am. Subdomains such as ORG, MIL, CO, and AC are also allowed.

The memo says MIL.AM is reserved by the Ministry of Defense and GOV.AM by the Government of Armenia. Other domains may be reserved for appropriate organizations by contacting the registry.
sections.plainLanguage: Organizations can register directly under .AM or use subdomains. The RFC names MIL.AM and GOV.AM as reserved.

sections.title: Delegation and Direct Registration
sections.content:
The RFC describes two registration types. Delegation gives a branch of the domain to an organization that operates name servers; direct registration puts information in the main database.

Direct registration may be for a host with an IP address or a non-IP host, such as a UUCP host. Applicants request and complete the AM second-level domain registration template and email it to the hostmaster for consideration.
sections.plainLanguage: An organization can run name servers for a delegated branch, or have its details entered in the main database. Applicants send the AM registration form by email.
